title: The Chainlog is a single on-chain registry of contract addresses whose updates ride along as housekeeping
content:
A.1.10.1.2 defines the Chainlog as "an on-chain, governance-managed registry that records the official addresses of Sky's core smart contracts," where "each contract entry... is identified by a unique key ('Chainlog key'), which is used to reference the contract in documentation, governance actions, and integrations. It serves as the single source of truth for contract addresses in the protocol."

The indirection layer is the point. Referring to contracts by stable key rather than by raw address means documentation, Spells, and third-party integrations do not need updating when a contract is replaced — and, more importantly, a reader of a governance proposal can tell *which* contract is meant without verifying a hex string by eye. Address confusion is a classic attack surface in on-chain governance, and a keyed registry removes most of it.

Being on-chain and governance-managed matters equally. An off-chain registry could be edited without a governance action; an on-chain one changes only through the Executive Process, so the mapping from key to address carries the same authority as any other protocol change.

The procedural detail is the interesting trade-off: "Updates to the Chainlog are defined as housekeeping items... and can be included directly in an Executive Vote." Registry maintenance therefore does not require its own proposal cycle — it rides along with whatever Spell is going out. That is sensible for genuine bookkeeping, since a registry that lags behind reality is worse than no registry.

But it is worth noting what the classification implies: a change to the authoritative key-to-address mapping is treated as routine. Since the Chainlog is what documentation, governance actions, and integrations resolve against, a wrong or malicious entry redirects everything that reads it — which makes the housekeeping path the lowest-scrutiny route to a high-leverage change, checked only by the general Spell review chain.
description: A.1.10.1.2 makes it the source of truth for Sky's core contract addresses, keyed for reference in documentation and integrations, with updates includable directly in an Executive Vote.
